lines.japanese: …………どこだ、ここ。
lines.english: ...Where am I?

lines.japanese: 吹き抜けの、やけにだだっ広い……ええと、オフィスビルの一階……に入ってるコーヒー屋か。
lines.english: An atrium. Ridiculously huge... Let's see. A coffee shop... on the ground floor of an office building?

lines.japanese: こんなとこに何の用だ、あいつ。つーか、今日はアレキサンダーじゃないのか。
lines.english: What the hell was he doing here? And wasn't he supposed to be at Alexander today?

lines.japanese: 俺は壁の洒落た時計を見た。２２時ちょっと前。
lines.english: I checked the stylish clock on the wall. Not quite ten.

lines.japanese: ほー、ここんとこ遅延続きだったあいつにしちゃ上出来だ。思わず笑みがこぼれる。俺は首と肩をほぐし、十本の指が自在に動くことを確かめた。
lines.english: Huh. Not bad, considering all his recent delays. A smile slipped out. I rolled my neck and shoulders loose, then checked that all ten fingers moved the way I wanted.

lines.japanese: ──よし、行こう。硬い椅子から立ちあがる。脇に置いてあったスポーツバッグを拾おうとしたとき、テーブルの上のコーヒーカップに気付いた。
lines.english: —Good. Let's go. I rose from the hard chair. Reaching for the sports bag beside me, I noticed the coffee cup on the table.

lines.japanese: カップには三口分ぐらいの茶色い液体が残っていた。その横に伝票と小銭が置いてある。それから、一冊の文庫本。
lines.english: Three sips or so of brown liquid remained. Beside the cup lay the check, some coins, and a paperback.

lines.japanese: 俺は本を手に取った。表紙は宮川書店の包装紙で覆われていた。一枚めくって中表紙を覗く。『ほほえみインサイド』。変なタイトル。すぐに閉じてバッグに突っこんだ。
lines.english: I picked up the book. Its cover was wrapped in paper from Miyagawa Books. I peeled back the wrapping and checked the title page. *Smile Inside*. Weird title. I closed it at once and shoved it into the bag.

lines.japanese: それからカップをあおって、残り少ない中身を一息で喉に流しこんだ。苦っ。砂糖足りねえよ。
lines.english: Then I tipped the cup back and drained what little remained in a single swallow. Bitter. Needed more sugar.

lines.japanese: 口の中に残った後味を恨めしく思いながら、俺は伝票とその代金を掴んだ。
lines.english: Cursing the aftertaste, I picked up the check and the money to pay it.

lines.japanese: 何がいいんだ、こんな豆汁。あいつ、無駄遣いしすぎなんじゃねえの。
lines.english: What did anybody see in this bean juice? That guy wasted way too much money.

lines.japanese: 適温に調整されたビルから出ると、冷たい夜風と静まりかえったオフィス街の景観が俺を迎えた。
lines.english: When I left the carefully climate-controlled building, a cold night wind and the hushed office district greeted me.

lines.japanese: ポケットに手を突っこんだままスキップするみたいに歩道へ下りて、くるっと体ごと振りあおいだ。かぁー、なんだこのデカくてオサレなビル。
lines.english: Hands still in my pockets, I stepped onto the sidewalk almost skipping, then turned and craned my whole body upward. Damn. What was this enormous, stylish building?

lines.japanese: つうかコレ、隣りも向かいも、あっちもそっちも。どこを向いても小奇麗な……いや、めっちゃ綺麗な、妙に光沢のある高層ビルが立ちならんでいた。
lines.english: And it wasn't just this one. The building next door, the one across the street, that one, that one too. Everywhere I looked stood trim—no, immaculate—high-rises with a peculiar sheen.

lines.japanese: 西を望めば、近未来の風を感じさせる厳かな官公庁のハイタワー。
lines.english: Look west: a solemn tower of government offices straight out of the near future.

lines.japanese: 東に向きなおれば、鉄道高架を挟んで毒々しいネオンサインやビルボード。
lines.english: Turn east: garish neon signs and billboards beyond the elevated tracks.

lines.japanese: 俺の帰るべき方角がどっちかは、言わなくても分かるよな。
lines.english: I don't have to tell you which way was home.

lines.japanese: 歩きながら、ポケットから紙切れを取りだした。
lines.english: As I walked, I pulled a scrap of paper from my pocket.

lines.japanese: ゆうべ漫喫でメモっておいた赤チャリ目撃情報を、常夜灯の明かりにさらす。
lines.english: Beneath a streetlight, I unfolded the reported sightings of the red bike that I'd copied down at the manga café last night.

lines.japanese: いくつか書きとめた中の──そうだな、まずは花水木通りの該当箇所を覗いてみるか。
lines.english: Of the places I'd written down... right. First I'd check the spot on Flowering Dogwood Street.

lines.japanese: こんなんで劇的に捜索効率が上がるわけは、まあ、ないんだろうけどさ。
lines.english: Not that this little trick was going to make the search suddenly efficient. Probably.

lines.japanese: 柳木原西口のオフィス街から、駅構内を経由して東口の繁華街へ向かう。
lines.english: From the office district at Yanagihara's west exit, I cut through the station toward the entertainment quarter on the east side.

lines.japanese: 見上げた吊り時計の長針が、１２と１のあいだに架かっていた。
lines.english: On the hanging clock overhead, the minute hand bridged twelve and one.

lines.japanese: 今夜もどこかでジェンベが鳴いている。
lines.english: Somewhere tonight, a djembe was crying again.

lines.japanese: 夜の街の玄関口では、きょうもマルチネスが露店を広げていた。
lines.english: At the gateway to the night streets, Martinez had set up his stall again.

lines.japanese: くたくたのテーラードジャケットにリュックの片側だけ背負った、およそアクセサリーとは縁遠そうな痩せぎすの男を捕まえて、黒い店主は執拗な営業トークを繰りひろげている。
lines.english: He'd cornered a skinny guy in a beat-up tailored jacket with a backpack hanging off one shoulder, a guy who looked like he had nothing to do with accessories. The Black shopkeeper was giving him the hard sell.

lines.japanese: 簡易ベンチの上。プラチナとアリスが、そんなマルチネスの仕事を見守れるポジションに陣取っていた──けど、少なくともいまは見守っていなかった。
lines.english: Platinum and Alice had staked out a spot on the makeshift bench where they could watch Martinez work—though right then neither of them was watching.

lines.japanese: 「ア、アイ、ワナビー、アクター！　ベリー、フェイマスアクター！　インザワールド！」
lines.english: “I, I wanna be actor! Very famous actor! In the world!”

lines.japanese: 「あなたは持つている夢。それはです、とても重要」
lines.english: “You have dream. It is very important.”

lines.japanese: 歳の離れた日本人とイギリス人のあいだでは、レベルの低そうな異文化コミュニケーションが交わされていた。
lines.english: A pretty rudimentary exercise in cross-cultural communication was under way between a Japanese man and a British girl many years his junior.

lines.japanese: 俺は近付いていって声をかけた。
lines.english: I approached and called out.

lines.japanese: 「なんの話」
lines.english: “What are you talking about?”

lines.japanese: 「わっ、ドラさん！？」
lines.english: “Whoa, Drac!?”

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、おはこんばんちは」
lines.english: “Drac, good-mornafterevening!”

lines.japanese: 金髪の子供は、得意げに右手を高く掲げて言った。
lines.english: The blond child raised her right hand high and proudly delivered the greeting.

lines.japanese: 「……あ？　ああ、えーと『こんばんは』」
lines.english: “...Huh? Oh. Right. ‘Good evening.’”

lines.japanese: 「あー、あのアリスさあ、言いにくいんだけど、その挨拶はちょっとやめた方がいいかも」
lines.english: Uh, hey, Alice... This is kinda hard to say, but maybe you oughta stop doing that greeting.

lines.japanese: 「ちがう。これ、りゅーこー語」
lines.english: “No. This is trendy word.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、まあ、流行語だった時代もあったんだけどな。ほら、言葉っつーのはナマ物だからさ」
lines.english: “Maybe once. Slang has a shelf life.”

lines.japanese: 俺は今日もアリスに日本語のベターな使い方を教えてやった。
lines.english: Once again, I gave Alice a lesson in better Japanese.

lines.japanese: こいつも、わざわざ夜遅くまでこんなとこいなくても、日本人のガキ共と明るいうちに隠れんぼとか鬼ごっことかして遊べばいいのにな。
lines.english: She could be out playing hide-and-seek or tag with Japanese kids while it was still light instead of hanging around a place like this so late.

lines.japanese: ま、それが出来ないからここにいるんだろうけど。
lines.english: Well, I guess that's why she was here.

lines.japanese: 「つか、なに夢って。いま夢がどうだか言ってなかった」
lines.english: “Anyway, what was that about a dream? You were talking about one, weren't you?”

lines.japanese: 「プラチナ願う、えいがすたあ世界の」
lines.english: “Platinum dream, become movie star in whole world.”

lines.japanese: 「映画スター？」
lines.english: “A movie star?”

lines.japanese: 視線をアリスからその隣りへ滑らせた。プラチナは照れくさそうに笑っていた。
lines.english: My gaze slid from Alice to the man beside her. Platinum smiled self-consciously.

lines.japanese: 「あー、やはは、子供は口が軽くて困りますね……」
lines.english: “Ha ha. Children really can't keep a secret...”

lines.japanese: 「え、おまえまだ役者ンなる気でいたの──」
lines.english: “Wait, you still thought you were going to be an actor—”

lines.japanese: 「──あ、ごめん、いまの言葉悪かった。ええと、そっちの方、まだ頑張ってたの」
lines.english: “—Sorry. That came out wrong. I mean, are you still working at it?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、ぼちぼち……と言ったところでしょうかね、はは」
lines.english: “Well, little by little... I suppose. Haha.”

lines.japanese: 本気で照れているのか、やつは乾いた笑いを続けるだけで、その話をまったく広げようとしない。
lines.english: Maybe he really was embarrassed. He just kept up that dry laugh and wouldn't say another word about it.

lines.japanese: 一方でアリスは、小さな白い手を、自分の喉元にかけた。
lines.english: Alice, meanwhile, placed one small white hand against her own throat.

lines.japanese: 「プラチナころす、られる。しめる、られるくび」
lines.english: “Platinum, he get killed. Neck get squeezed.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なにそれ。なに殺されるって」
lines.english: “Huh? What's that? What do you mean, killed?”

lines.japanese: 「こらっ、もうアリス！」
lines.english: “Hey! Enough, Alice!”

lines.japanese: プラチナは子供相手に怒鳴りつけるわけにもいかず、教育番組のおにいさんみたいに腰へ手を置いて頬を膨らませてみせた。
lines.english: Unable to shout at a child, Platinum planted his hands on his hips and puffed his cheeks like the big brother who hosted a children’s educational show.

lines.japanese: しかしそれは、欧米人に通用しないジェスチャーだったみたいだ。アリスは目をぱちくりさせてから、面白そうにその身振りを真似した。ぷっぷくぷー。
lines.english: Apparently the gesture didn’t translate for Westerners. Alice blinked, then copied him with evident delight. Puffity-puff.

lines.japanese: 「おう、だからなんだよ殺されるって」
lines.english: “Hey, so what is this about getting killed?”

lines.japanese: 「い、いえ、そのう……本当は放映日が近付いてから、さりげなく言おうと思ってたんですが」
lines.english: “N-no, well... I was planning to mention it casually once the broadcast date got closer.”

lines.japanese: 「実はこの前、オーディションに受かっちゃいまして。ま、サスペンスドラマのチョイ役なんですけどね」
lines.english: “The truth is, I passed an audition the other day. It's only a bit part in a suspense drama.”

lines.japanese: 「サスペンスドラマ……え、出んの」
lines.english: “A suspense drama... You're going to be in it?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ……まあ、そういうことですよね……はは」
lines.english: “Well... yes. I suppose that's what it means... Ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 「うそ、すげえじゃん。え、マジすげえじゃん」
lines.english: “No way. That's amazing. No, seriously—that's incredible.”

lines.japanese: 「ぷー」
lines.english: “Pff.”

lines.japanese: アリスも膨らませたほっぺたから息を吹きだしながら頷いた。
lines.english: Alice nodded too, letting the air escape from her puffed cheeks.

lines.japanese: 「ややや、もうそんなふたりとも、やめてよ、やめてくださいよ」
lines.english: N-no, no, come on, you two, stop it! Please, stop!

lines.japanese: 「いや、ほんとにチョイ役なんですよ、お恥ずかしい。ささっと出てきて、きゅきゅっと死ぬだけです」
lines.english: No, really, it's just a bit part. It's embarrassing. I pop in quick, get choked out quick, and that's it.

lines.japanese: 「画面だってどうせ、首絞めてる女優さんのアップですし。僕なんて終始ほとんど、声だけですよ声だけ、はは、声というより悲鳴かな」
lines.english: “Besides, the camera will be tight on the actress strangling me. For nearly the whole scene, I'll be nothing but a voice. A voice, ha ha—or more of a scream, maybe.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、でも声だけって、だってソレ逆に難しくね？」
lines.english: “But doing it with just your voice has to be harder, doesn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「ぷー」
lines.english: “Pff.”

lines.japanese: 「だろ？　すげえよプラチナ。おまえ来てるって、スターの風来てるって」
lines.english: Right? This is huge, Platinum. You're on your way. I can feel the star power coming!

lines.japanese: 「わたしは同意する。かれはとても夢をちかづいた」
lines.english: “I agree. He become much closer to dream.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょーちょー、どんな芝居なのソレ。ちょっと見せろよ、いま」
lines.english: “Wait, wait—what kind of acting is it? Show us. Right now.”

lines.japanese: 「え、えええ？　そんな、勘弁してくださいよ。全然です本当、まだまだ大根もいいところです」
lines.english: “Wh-what!? Please, spare me. I’m terrible. A complete ham, honestly.”

lines.japanese: 「しかし、あなたはたちどころに嬉しそうだ」
lines.english: “But now, you look suddenly happy.”

lines.japanese: 「よし。じゃあアリス、おまえ加害者やれ。こいつの首きゅっと絞めろ。はいヨーイ、カチン」
lines.english: “Good. Alice, you're the killer. Give his neck a quick squeeze. Ready... clack!”

lines.japanese: 「や、カチンじゃなくて、僕まだ仕事中だしこんなところで──」
lines.english: “Wait, not ‘clack.’ I'm still working, and we're in public—”

lines.japanese: 「きゅ」
lines.english: “Squeeze.”

lines.japanese: 「んくぅぅぅ！　て、てめえ……ハメやがったな……あ、か、かふっ……」
lines.english: “Nghhhh! Y-you... you set me up... Ah—khh...”

lines.japanese: 「うぉスゲ、迫真の演技じゃん。チョーもがき苦しンでんじゃん」
lines.english: “Whoa, incredible. That’s seriously convincing. You’re really writhing in agony.”

lines.japanese: 「だましたネー。わたしの心。もてあそんだネー」
lines.english: “You tricked me. Toyed with my heart.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、ごめん、そういう筋じゃないんだ」
lines.english: “Ah, sorry. That isn't the plot.”

lines.japanese: 「ばか、おまえ生きかえんなよ。アドリブの利かねーやつだな、事務所どこだよ」
lines.english: “Idiot, don’t come back to life. You can’t improvise for shit. Who even represents you?”

lines.japanese: 「ええー、何この監督！」
lines.english: “What is *with* this director!?”

lines.japanese: 「かんとく、共犯。かんとく、いっしょにころす」
lines.english: “Director is accomplice. Director kill too.”

lines.japanese: アリスが俺の裾をくいくい引っぱるから、俺は急遽、加害者の夫役として乱入することになった。
lines.english: Alice kept tugging at my hem, so I was hastily drafted into the scene as the murderer's husband.

lines.japanese: 「おらー、若造ー。てめえかー、アリ子の縦笛盗んだのはー。ばきゅんといっちゃうぞコノヤロー。あ、ばきゅんっと」
lines.english: “Hey, punk! You're the bastard who stole Allie's recorder! I'll put a bullet in you! Bang—there, bang!”

lines.japanese: 「あ゛ああっ！　が、ぐ、ぐ……」
lines.english: “Aaaagh! G-guh, guh...”

lines.japanese: 空想ピストルをブッ放すと、プラチナは胸を掴み、額に苦悶の皺をきざんだ。
lines.english: When I fired the imaginary pistol, Platinum clutched his chest and his brow furrowed in agony.

lines.japanese: あまりの凄絶な眼光に一瞬寒気すら覚えたが、すぐにそれはとても心地の良い高揚感を呼びさました。
lines.english: For an instant, the terrible intensity in his eyes actually chilled me. Then it stirred a deep and strangely pleasant excitement.

lines.japanese: 「すげえ。かっちぇー。おお、なんか俺、あったかい気持ちンなってきたよ。超わくわくしてきた」
lines.english: “Incredible. So cool. Wow, I feel all warm inside. This is seriously exciting.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、ですから！　そういう筋じゃないんですよ！」
lines.english: “I keep telling you! That isn't the plot!”

lines.japanese: いい歳して子供みたいにはしゃぎ回る俺たちを、駅前広場に集う暇人たちが白い目で見ていた。
lines.english: The idlers gathered in the station plaza gave us cold looks. We were old enough to know better and still carrying on like children.

lines.japanese: その中には刃物のように鋭い眼光さえあった。
lines.english: Among them was one gaze sharp as a blade.

lines.japanese: 俺は気付かないふりをした。ほっとけ。こちとら、今夜はめでたいプラチナ祭りだ。
lines.english: I pretended not to notice. Leave us alone. Tonight was the glorious Platinum Festival.

lines.japanese: 「実はちょっと前、実家に手紙を書いたんです。メールじゃないですよ、手紙ですよ？　ええ、コンビニでレターセットと切手を買ってきて」
lines.english: “Actually, a little while ago, I wrote home. Not an email—a letter. I bought stationery and a stamp at the convenience store.”

lines.japanese: アリスをタクシー乗り場まで見送ったあと、プラチナはまだ誰にも口外していない（しかし今後はあらゆる顔見知りに語りまくることだろう）という話を始めた。
lines.english: After seeing Alice to the taxi stand, Platinum started telling me something he'd never told anyone before (though from here on out, he'd probably blab it to everyone he knew).

lines.japanese: 「僕ほら、勘当されてるって言ったでしょう。家族の反対押しきって家を飛びだしたもので……あ、飛びだすってこれ、比喩表現じゃありません。リアルで二階の窓から飛びおりました」
lines.english: “I told you I was disowned, right? I flew the coop against my family’s wishes... Oh, and when I say flew, I mean it. I actually jumped out of a second-story window.”

lines.japanese: 「それ以来、連絡一本しないまま五年ですからね。何の弁解もないですよ、両親の怒りはもっともです。いちおう地元の友人なんかを介して、死んじゃいないことだけは伝わってたようですが」
lines.english: “Five years since then without a single word from me. I've got no defense. My parents had every right to be angry. Apparently friends back home at least let them know I wasn't dead.”

lines.japanese: 「へー。それで手紙ってのは」
lines.english: “Huh. So the letter?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、やっぱり、電話じゃ切られてしまうんじゃないかと思って。逆に怒鳴りちらされる勇気もなかったですしね。もちろんメアドなんか知りませんし、だったらまあ、手紙……かなあと」
lines.english: “Well, I thought they might hang up if I called. And I wasn’t exactly brave enough to risk being screamed at. Naturally, I didn’t know their email addresses. So I thought... maybe a letter.”

lines.japanese: 手紙の内容を聞いたつもりだったが「手紙という伝達手段を選んだ理由」ではぐらかされてしまった。詳しいことは話したくないんだろうか──
lines.english: I'd meant to ask what the letter said, but he'd fobbed me off with an explanation of why he'd chosen to write one. Maybe he didn't want to go into the details—

lines.japanese: ──いや、そんなはずはない。これはプラチナが自分からおっ始めた話だ。俺はふうんと呟いてから、もう一度訊ねてやった。
lines.english: —No, impossible. Platinum had started this story himself. I murmured *huh,* then obligingly asked again.

lines.japanese: 「で。なんて書いたの」
lines.english: “So. What did you write?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、なに書いたっけなぁ……とりあえず、こっちは適当に生きてるけどそっちはどうよ！　みたいな？」
lines.english: “Hmm. What *did* I write...? Something like, I’m muddling along over here—how about you?”

lines.japanese: やつは照れくさそうにおどけた。
lines.english: Embarrassed, he turned it into a joke.

lines.japanese: 「五年ぶりにしちゃ軽いな」
lines.english: “Pretty breezy after five years.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、いえいえ、もちろん実際の文面は真面目に書きましたよ？　ネットで手紙の書き方なんて調べながら、馬鹿丁寧に前略おふくろ様ですよ」
lines.english: “Ha ha. No, no, naturally the actual wording was serious. I looked up how to write a letter online and went absurdly formal. Full-on *Dear Mother, forgive the abruptness.*”

lines.japanese: 「で、一応まあ、すみませんでしたと。あの頃は自分もガキでしたと。少しは大人になった今、おふたりの愛情に気付くことができ、深く深く猛省しておりますと──」
lines.english: “I apologized, for one thing. Said I'd been a child then. That now I'd grown up a little, I could recognize their love and felt the deepest, most profound remorse—”

lines.japanese: 「──あ、さすがに仕事の話は書けませんでしたけどね、ははは」
lines.english: “—Though I couldn't bring myself to write about my work, obviously. Hahaha.”

lines.japanese: 俺はまたふうんと言った。
lines.english: I said *huh* again.

lines.japanese: 「それ出したのって、いつの話」
lines.english: “When did you send it?”

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、もう半年ぐらい前の話です」
lines.english: “Oh, that was around six months ago.”

lines.japanese: 「返事は来たの」
lines.english: “Did they answer?”

lines.japanese: 「速かったですよ。しかも現金書留で。父には内緒でと書きそえて、万札が三枚入っていました」
lines.english: “Fast. She sent registered cash, no less. She added a note saying not to tell my father and enclosed three ten-thousand-yen bills.”

lines.japanese: 「参っちゃいますよね。どうも母は、食うに困った家出息子が金の無心で手紙をよこしたと思ったみたいで。うーん、僕はかなり本気で謝罪文をしたためたつもりだったんですけど、その件はほとんど無視ですもん」
lines.english: “Enough to floor you, isn't it? Apparently my mother thought her runaway son was starving and had written to beg for money. I meant it as a serious letter of apology, but she practically ignored that part.”

lines.japanese: 「なにせ、叱りの言葉がひとつもないんですね。ただ野菜を摂れとか、医者代ケチるなとか……とにかく元気でいろと言うようなことばかり、便箋十枚に渡って延々と書かれていて」
lines.english: “Not one word of scolding. Just *eat your vegetables* and *don't pinch pennies on doctor bills*... Ten whole sheets, all of it telling me above everything to stay healthy.”

lines.japanese: 「母の五年分の愛だろ、そりゃおまえ、一行や二行じゃ収まんねえよ」
lines.english: “That's five years of a mother's love. Of course it won't fit into a line or two.”

lines.japanese: 「でも僕、勘当されたんですよ？　家を飛びだすときだって、ちょっと……」
lines.english: “But I was disowned. And when I left home, I said some... well...”

lines.japanese: 「その、なんて言いますか……要は、僕のうち貧乏だったんで……ハハ、恩知らずなひどいこと、いっぱい怒鳴りつけちゃって……」
lines.english: “How do I put it? My family was poor... Ha ha. I screamed all kinds of awful, ungrateful things at them...”

lines.japanese: 社会の荒波に揉まれまくった若者は、かつて糞ガキだった時代に吐いてしまった暴言を思いおこして、心底不快そうに顔を歪めていた。
lines.english: Buffeted relentlessly by the rough seas of society, the young man remembered the abuse he’d hurled as a rotten little brat, his face twisting in disgust at himself.

lines.japanese: 「でも良かったじゃん。お袋さんはもう許してくれたっつーことだろ」
lines.english: “But that’s good, isn’t it? It means your mom already forgave you.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえ、ところが──」
lines.english: “Ah, no. The thing is—”

lines.japanese: 「──僕の父は、テレビといえばニュースと野球と園芸教室しか観ないようなひとだったんです。それなのに僕が出ていったあと、中古のでかいプラズマを買ってきて、暇さえあればドラマを点けてるって言うんです」
lines.english: “My father was the kind of man who only ever watched the news, baseball, and gardening shows. But after I left, he bought a huge secondhand plasma TV and now, apparently, leaves dramas on whenever he has a spare moment.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ……え、それはなんで」
lines.english: “Huh...? Why would he do that?”

lines.japanese: 「なんででしょうねえ。こう、番組の主題歌やエンディングテーマが流れだすとね、新聞紙で顔を隠しながら、じっと横目で画面を見てるらしいんですよ。まさか親不幸息子の名前でも探してるわけじゃないですよねえ」
lines.english: “Who knows? Apparently, whenever a show's opening or ending theme starts, he hides behind the newspaper and watches the screen from the corner of his eye. Surely he isn't searching the credits for the name of his unfilial son.”

lines.japanese: 俺は信号を待ちながら、頬の裏側を舌先で尖らせた。
lines.english: Waiting for the light, I pushed the tip of my tongue into the inside of my cheek.

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、今年の暮は田舎帰れば」
lines.english: “Why don't you go home for New Year's?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、まあ……そうなんですよね……」
lines.english: “Yes, well... I suppose I should...”

lines.japanese: やつははにかみながら「敷居またがせてくれるかなあ」とつぶやいた。
lines.english: With a bashful smile, he murmured, “I wonder if they'll even let me cross the threshold.”

lines.japanese: 「実はもう、放映日に合わせて夜行バスのチケットを取ってあるんです」
lines.english: “Actually, I’ve already booked an overnight bus for the day the show airs.”

lines.japanese: 「夜行バス？」
lines.english: “An overnight bus?”

lines.japanese: 湯水のように金を使う男が、飛行機でも新幹線でもなく、夜行バス。
lines.english: A man who poured money away like water. No plane. No bullet train. An overnight bus.

lines.japanese: 「なに。倹約」
lines.english: “What, economizing now?”

lines.japanese: 「倹約……ええ、そうですね。これからはちょっと倹約しようと思って」
lines.english: “Economizing... Yes. That's right. I thought I should start saving a little from now on.”

lines.japanese: 冷やかしたつもりが、意外にも正解だったらしい。やつは照れくさそうに髪を梳いた。
lines.english: I’d only meant to rib him, but apparently I’d guessed right. Looking embarrassed, he ran a hand through his hair.

lines.japanese: 「実はもうスカウトの仕事やめることにしました。ほら、おととい、メンマさんの店で会ったでしょう。あのときは僕、お世話になった方々への挨拶回りをしてきた帰りだったんです」
lines.english: “The truth is, I've decided to quit working as a scout. Remember when we met at Menma's place the night before last? I was on my way back from making the rounds to say goodbye to everyone who'd helped me.”

lines.japanese: あの晩、プラチナは顔にデカい痣をこしらえていた（いまもその名残がうっすら青く滲んでいる）。しかし、にも関わらず、気味悪いぐらいのハイテンションだった。
lines.english: That night, Platinum had worn one hell of a bruise across his face. Its last traces still showed in faint blue today. Yet despite it, he'd been in almost unnervingly high spirits.

lines.japanese: 享楽の日々を捨て、ふたたび夢に向かって歩きはじめた第一歩。こいつにとってはそんな夜だったのかもしれない。
lines.english: Casting off his days of pleasure. Taking the first step back toward his dream. Maybe that was what the night had meant to him.

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ、勿体つけて。つまりあんとき、すでに綺麗なエピローグが付いてたんじゃん」
lines.english: “Why’d you make such a mystery of it? So that night already came with its own neat little epilogue.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、やだなあエピローグって。勝手にひとの人生たたまないでくださいよ」
lines.english: “Ha ha, don't call it an epilogue. You can't just fold up a man's life without asking him.”

lines.japanese: 俺の冷やかしにも堪えず、やつは浮かれたように笑っていた。
lines.english: My teasing didn't faze him. He only laughed, giddy with happiness.

lines.japanese: もっとも、本人言うところの職業病のせいで、プラチナはいつでもだいたい営業スマイルを浮かべているやつなんだけれど。
lines.english: Then again, thanks to what he called an occupational hazard, Platinum wore a salesman’s smile more or less all the time.

lines.japanese: でも、もしかしたら俺たちはいままで、ずっとこいつの名演技に騙されつづけてきたのかもしれない。
lines.english: But perhaps all this time we'd simply been taken in by one magnificent performance.

lines.japanese: 金と女だけが生き甲斐の、悩みなんか何ひとつない気楽な男だってみんな笑ってた。
lines.english: We'd all laughed at him as a carefree man with nothing to live for but money and women, without a worry in the world.

lines.japanese: でも本当は、飽くなき夢を秘めたまま絶えず泣いたり悩んだり頑張ったりして、だけどそんな格好悪い自分を見せたくないから、派手に着飾った都会の色男を演じていただけなのかもしれない──
lines.english: Maybe the truth was that he’d carried an insatiable dream inside him, forever crying and worrying and struggling for it—and because he couldn’t bear to let anyone see that unglamorous side of himself, he’d simply played the gaudy, overdressed ladies’ man from the big city—

lines.japanese: ──なんて、それはちょっと美談が過ぎるか。
lines.english: —Though perhaps that made it too pretty a story.

lines.japanese: でも、半分ぐらいは当たってると思わないか？
lines.english: Still. Don't you think at least half of it was true?

lines.japanese: 格好いいやと思った。
lines.english: I thought he was pretty damn cool.

lines.japanese: 横断歩道を渡ったあと、プラチナの体当たりの演技が見られるチャンネルと放映日時を聞いて、それから俺たちはいつかのように左右へ別れた。
lines.english: After we’d crossed the street, I asked which channel and what time I could see Platinum throw his whole body into the role. Then, as once before, we went our separate ways.

lines.japanese: 混みあった歩道を進もうとしたが、ふと言いわすれたことを思いだして踵を返した。
lines.english: I started down the crowded sidewalk, then remembered something I'd forgotten to say and spun on my heel.

lines.japanese: 「ちょーちょー、おう未来のスター」
lines.english: “Hey, hold up! Yo, future star!”

lines.japanese: 若草色の背中に声をかけると、雑踏の中でその後ろ姿がぴたりと止まった。
lines.english: I called to the pale-green back, and it stopped dead amid the crowd.

lines.japanese: 「いま僕を呼んだかいハニー？」
lines.english: “Did you call for me, honey?”

lines.japanese: そして振りむきざま、指を鳴らす流れで俺に人差し指を向けた。
lines.english: He spun around, snapped his fingers, and finished the flourish with one index finger pointed straight at me.

lines.japanese: はた迷惑なオーバーアクションに、行きかう通行人まで一緒になって俺たちを見上げたり振りむいたりした。しわくちゃのチューリップ帽だけが俯いたまま人ごみに溶けこんでいた。
lines.english: His obnoxious overacting made passing pedestrians look over at us too. Only one crumpled tulip hat kept its head bowed and melted into the crowd.

lines.japanese: 「あのさー。おみやげは温泉まんじゅうでいいから」
lines.english: “Just so you know, hot-spring buns are fine for my souvenir.”

lines.japanese: 群集の頭を数個挟んだ距離で言うと、プラチナはサニーブラウンの二枚目ヅラに白い歯を覗かせた。
lines.english: I called across the several heads between us. Platinum flashed white teeth in his handsome, sun-browned face.

lines.japanese: 「はいはい」
lines.english: “Yes, yes.”

lines.japanese: そして俺はまっすぐ目潰しピースを向ける。
lines.english: And I aimed two fingers straight at his eyes.

lines.japanese: 「元クソガキ。親孝行してこいよ」
lines.english: “Former little shit. Go do right by your parents.”

lines.japanese: やつも右手を上げて俺の真似をした。
lines.english: He raised his right hand and mirrored me.

lines.japanese: 「ドラさんこそ、好きな子できたんだから、そろそろニート卒業しましょうよ」
lines.english: “And you, Drac—you've found a girl you like. Isn't it about time you graduated from being an unemployed shut-in?”
“...The hell?”

lines.japanese: 参った。
lines.english: He had me.

lines.japanese: そういやプラチナは、そういう方面の観察眼がおそろしく発達したやつだった。
lines.english: Come to think of it, Platinum had a terrifyingly sharp eye for that sort of thing.

lines.japanese: 「ドラさん、ちょっと名残惜しいですけど、僕はもう行きますよ」
lines.english: “Drac, I hate to go, but it’s time.”

lines.japanese: 「楽しくて気持ちのいい冬休みが、ずいぶん長く続きました。ずっとここにいたい気持ちも、もちろんあります。でももう行きますね。辛いと思うけど、やっぱり僕は自分の目指した先へ進んでみせます」
lines.english: “It's been a long winter vacation. Fun and comfortable, and far longer than I expected. Of course part of me wants to stay here forever. But I'm going now. I know it will hurt, but I'm still going to press on toward the place I once set my sights on.”

lines.japanese: 笑っていないやつの顔を、俺はまるで初めて見た気がした。
lines.english: I felt as though I were seeing Platinum's face without a smile for the first time.

lines.japanese: 若草色のスーツの頭上、街頭ビジョンの向こう側で、缶ビールのプルタブが音高く引きあげられた。泡立つ黄金色は巨大な四辺形を埋めつくし、色とりどりの街明かりと溶けあってやつの背中に後光を与える。
lines.english: Above the pale-green suit, on a street-side video screen, the pull tab of a beer can cracked loudly open. Foaming gold flooded the colossal rectangle, mingled with the many-colored city lights, and cast a halo over his back.

lines.japanese: 「ドラさん、お先に失礼します」
lines.english: “Drac, I’ll be off, then.”

lines.japanese: プラチナはプラチナ色に輝いていた。
lines.english: Platinum shone platinum.

lines.japanese: 「なあ。次会うときは俺ら、お互いちょっとぐれー成長してたりして」
lines.english: “Hey. Next time we meet, maybe we'll both have grown up a little.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、そしたら僕、ドラさんに記念すべき一枚目のサインをあげますよ」
lines.english: “Ha ha. Then I’ll give you the very first autograph of my career, Drac.”

lines.japanese: 「おー。楽しみにしてるわ」
lines.english: “Yeah. I'll look forward to it.”

lines.japanese: そうして俺たちは今度こそ別れた。
lines.english: And with that, this time, we really did part.

lines.japanese: 本当に別れた。
lines.english: We really parted.
